title: The Reincorporation That Kept Everything But the EIN
scenario_text: Dallington Retail's customer success team is building the renewal package for an enterprise SaaS customer and needs the correct total ARR at risk in a single renewal. The customer shows up as two records. Salesforce Account A: "Brightside Retail LLC" (account BR-1002, created 2019, status set to Inactive on 2023-07-01, tax ID 83-2214477, subscription ARR $300,000). Salesforce Account B: "Brightside Retail, Inc." (account BR-2210, created 2023-07, status Active, tax ID 88-9910022, subscription ARR $240,000 from add-on analytics and API modules). A CSM note on Account B reads: "Customer completed a Delaware statutory conversion from an LLC to a C-corporation effective 2023-07-01 (an F-reorganization); a new EIN was issued on conversion, but it is the same business, same people, same subscription - not a new customer." Ironclad holds a single master subscription agreement, originally signed 2019, amended 2023-07 to update the counterparty legal name from "Brightside Retail LLC" to "Brightside Retail, Inc." while preserving the same agreement number, the same order-form lineage, and one continuous, co-terminous subscription term ending 2025-03-31. Billing in Stripe moved to a new customer object on conversion but references the same subscription ID and the same purchase-order chain. Support tickets and usage telemetry continued without interruption across the conversion date. The renewal is a single co-terminous event covering the entire subscription.
question: What total ARR should the single renewal package show as at risk for this customer?
